title: Cycles in a Shuffle
statement: A permutation of $\{1,\dots,10\}$ is chosen uniformly at random. What is the expected number of cycles in it? (Fixed points count as cycles of length 1.)
insight: Build the permutation by following a cycle: at each step, the next element closes the current cycle with probability 1/(remaining).
redHerring: Counting permutations by cycle type with Stirling numbers.
hints: Generate the permutation by tracing cycles: start at 1 and follow $i \to \pi(i)$.
When $k$ elements are still unused (including the current cycle's start), what is the chance the next step closes the cycle?
solution:
Trace cycles: start at the smallest unused element and repeatedly choose its image among the $k$ elements still available, one of which is the cycle's start. Choosing the start closes the cycle, with probability $\tfrac1k$. $k$ runs through $10, 9, \dots, 1$, so

$E[\#\text{cycles}] = \sum_{k=1}^{10}\tfrac1k = H_{10} = \tfrac{7381}{2520}\approx 2.929$.
